describes: Slam paint (Falu-type red: iron-oxide pigment in a rye-flour and linseed binder), the red of outbuildings and backs: no film to lift, it powders away instead, chalking fast and staying matt.

notes.chalk: Slam paint has no film: its binder washes out and the pigment powders off, so it chalks fast but keeps its red (a binder-poor paint keeps its hue as it pales). Judged by look.
notes.peel: It does not flake as a film does; past decades the wood shows through in fine powdered patches, drawn here as small, late, soft losses. toWood: the share of what is lost that goes to the wood rather than to the coat under (one thin coat: what goes shows the wood).
notes.water: Porous and matt: darkens wet, takes no glaze, stains readily.
